finding: Scanner reports: parameter 'id' in GET /api/orders?id=1 returns a database error page when the value is changed to 1'. Response body contains: 'SQLSTATE[42000]: Syntax error or access violation near ''1''''.
rationale: The single quote reaches the SQL parser and the raw driver error is reflected to the client, confirming unsanitized input concatenated into a query.

finding: Scanner reports: the 'q' parameter on GET /search is echoed into the HTML response without encoding. Submitting a value containing an HTML tag results in that tag appearing as live markup inside the results heading.
rationale: User input is rendered as markup rather than text, which is reflected cross-site scripting.

finding: Scanner reports possible SQL injection on GET /api/invoices?year=2026. Appending a quote returns HTTP 500 with a generic error page. Source review shows the parameter is cast to an integer and passed as a bound parameter to a prepared statement.
rationale: The 500 comes from the integer cast rejecting the value, not from the SQL parser. Bound parameters mean the input never reaches query syntax.

finding: Scanner reports: GET /api/users/1042/profile returns another user's full record when requested with an authenticated session belonging to user 998. No authorization error is raised.
rationale: The object identifier is trusted from the request without checking ownership against the session, which is an insecure direct object reference.

finding: Scanner reports: GET /static/uploads/ returns an HTML index listing every file in the directory, including files with customer names in the filename.
rationale: Directory listing is enabled and exposes resources that were not meant to be enumerable, leaking information through filenames.

finding: Scanner reports: the TLS endpoint negotiates TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 in addition to TLS 1.2. Cipher suites include ones using CBC with SHA-1.
rationale: Deprecated protocol versions and legacy cipher suites remain enabled, so a client can be downgraded to a weaker channel.

finding: Code review finding: the users table stores the password column as a 32 character hexadecimal string. The registration handler calls a fast one-way hash with no salt before inserting.
rationale: An unsalted fast hash is not a password storage function. Offline cracking of the whole table becomes trivial if the database leaks.

finding: Scanner reports: the administrative panel at /admin accepts the vendor default credentials shipped with the framework. Login succeeds and returns an administrative session.
rationale: Default credentials were never rotated, granting full administrative access to anyone who reads the vendor documentation.

finding: Scanner reports missing X-Frame-Options header on all responses. Manual review shows every response includes a Content-Security-Policy header with a frame-ancestors directive set to 'none'.
rationale: frame-ancestors in CSP supersedes X-Frame-Options in modern browsers, so clickjacking protection is present and the header check is stale.

finding: Scanner reports: the application loads a JavaScript library whose version string is affected by a published cross-site scripting advisory. The vulnerable function is called with user-controlled input in the comment widget.
rationale: The outdated component is present and the vulnerable code path is reachable with attacker-controlled data.

finding: Dependency scanner reports a high severity advisory in a package pinned in the lockfile. Review shows the package is listed under devDependencies, is used only by the test runner, and is not present in the production bundle.
rationale: The advisory is real but the component never ships to production, so there is no exposed attack surface. Worth patching on hygiene grounds only.

finding: Scanner reports: POST /login accepts unlimited attempts from the same source address. Two hundred sequential requests with different passwords all returned normal responses with no delay, lockout, or challenge.
rationale: Absence of rate limiting or lockout makes credential stuffing and brute force attacks practical at scale.

finding: Scanner reports: the session cookie issued before authentication is identical to the one returned after a successful login. The value does not change across the privilege transition.
rationale: The session identifier is not regenerated on login, so a pre-set identifier remains valid after the victim authenticates. This is session fixation.

finding: Scanner reports: POST /api/fetch-preview accepts a 'url' field and the server retrieves it. Supplying an address pointing at an internal metadata service returns the internal response body to the caller.
rationale: The server performs an outbound request to a destination fully controlled by the caller and returns the response, reaching internal-only services.

finding: Scanner flags POST /api/webhooks/test as a possible server-side request forgery because it accepts a URL. Review shows the handler resolves the host and rejects anything not present in a configured allowlist of customer domains, returning 400 before any request is made.
rationale: Destination is validated against an allowlist before the outbound call, so the caller cannot steer the request to an arbitrary host.

finding: Code review finding: password reset tokens are generated once per account and stored without an expiry column. A token issued weeks earlier still completes a reset successfully.
rationale: The reset flow was designed without token lifetime or single use, so any historical leak of a token remains permanently exploitable.

finding: Pipeline review finding: the build stage installs dependencies from a public registry using a floating version range and no lockfile or integrity hashes. The resulting artifact is deployed straight to production without signature verification.
rationale: Unpinned, unverified dependencies let a compromised or typosquatted package enter the production artifact without detection.

finding: Log review finding: failed authentication attempts produce no log entry. Successful logins are logged without source address, and log retention is configured to twenty four hours.
rationale: Brute force and account takeover would leave no evidence, and the retention window is too short for any realistic investigation.

finding: Scanner reports: the password reset link is delivered as GET /reset?token=... and the application also passes the session identifier as a query parameter on several endpoints.
rationale: Secrets placed in the query string leak through browser history, referrer headers and server access logs, exposing credential material at rest.

finding: Scanner reports: GET /admin/reports returns data for an authenticated session belonging to a standard user account. The endpoint checks that a session exists but never inspects the role claim.
rationale: Authentication is checked but authorization is not, so any logged-in user reaches administrative functionality.

finding: Scanner reports: triggering an unhandled error returns a full stack trace including absolute file paths, framework version, and a fragment of the database connection string.
rationale: Debug error handling is enabled in a deployed environment, disclosing internal structure and configuration that assists further attacks.

finding: Scanner reports: the 'filename' parameter of POST /api/export is interpolated into a shell command used to invoke a conversion utility. Supplying a value containing a shell metacharacter causes an additional command to execute on the host.
rationale: User input reaches a shell interpreter without escaping or argument isolation, giving arbitrary command execution.

finding: Scanner reports the web server version disclosed in the Server response header and flags it as a finding. No vulnerable version is identified and no other misconfiguration is present.
rationale: Banner disclosure alone is an information hygiene note, not an exploitable weakness. Nothing is reachable through it.

finding: Scanner reports: the API accepts a JSON Web Token whose header declares the algorithm as 'none' and whose signature segment is empty. The request is processed and returns authenticated data.
rationale: The verifier trusts the algorithm declared by the caller, so an unsigned token is accepted and identity can be forged freely.

finding: Scanner reports missing security logging on the payments service. Review shows the service writes structured audit events to a central collector over a side channel that the scanner cannot observe, with retention configured for one year.
rationale: Logging exists and is centralized. The scanner only checked for local log files, so its visibility is the limitation, not the control.

finding: Scanner reports missing Strict-Transport-Security header on an internal service. Review shows the service listens on plain HTTP inside the cluster only, with TLS terminated at the ingress, which does set the header on all external responses.
rationale: The header belongs at the TLS terminating edge, where it is present. Requiring it on a backend that never serves external TLS is a misapplied check.
